questions.question: Which metal reacts violently with cold water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium** is a highly reactive metal belonging to **Group 1** (alkali metals) of the **Periodic Table** with an **atomic number** of **11**.
 
• It reacts **violently** and **explosively** with **cold water** to produce **sodium hydroxide** and **hydrogen gas**. The reaction is represented as **2Na + 2H2O → 2NaOH + H2**.
 
• The reaction is extremely **exothermic**, meaning it releases a significant amount of heat. This heat is often sufficient to ignite the **hydrogen gas** produced, leading to a visible flame or explosion. ***Hence, the statement regarding sodium reacting violently with cold water is correct.***
 
• Due to its high reactivity with both **oxygen** and **moisture** (water vapor) in the air, **sodium** is always stored under **kerosene oil** to prevent accidental reactions.
 
• **Potassium** is another metal that reacts even more violently than sodium with cold water, as reactivity increases down the group in the periodic table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Magnesium (Mg):**

 
 
• **Magnesium** has the **atomic number 12** and belongs to **Group 2** (alkaline earth metals).
 
• It does **not react** with **cold water**. However, it reacts slowly with **hot water** and more vigorously with **steam** to form magnesium hydroxide and hydrogen. ***Hence, the statement that magnesium reacts violently with cold water is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Aluminium (Al):**
 
 
• **Aluminium** is a metal in **Group 13** with the **atomic number 13**.
 
• It does not react with **cold or hot water** under normal conditions due to the formation of a tough, protective **oxide layer** on its surface. It only reacts with **steam** at high temperatures. ***Hence, the statement regarding aluminium is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Copper (Cu):**
 
 
• **Copper** is a transition metal with the **atomic number 29**.
 
• It is placed very low in the **reactivity series**, even below **hydrogen**. Consequently, it does **not react** with water or steam at any temperature. ***Hence, the statement regarding copper is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Reactivity Series:**
 
 
• The **reactivity series** is a list of metals arranged in the order of their **decreasing chemical reactivity**.
 
• Metals like **Potassium, Sodium, Lithium, and Calcium** are at the top and can react with cold water. Metals like **Gold, Silver, and Platinum** are at the bottom and are highly unreactive.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chemical Hazards:** Handling **Sodium** requires strict safety protocols, including the use of **forceps** and protective gear, as skin contact can cause severe **chemical burns** due to the reaction with moisture on the skin.
 
• **Density:** Sodium is one of the few metals that is **less dense than water** (density approx **0.97 g/cm3**). Because of this, it **floats** on the surface of the water while it reacts violently, moving around rapidly as the hydrogen gas is evolved.
 
• **Identification:** When sodium reacts with water, the resulting solution of **sodium hydroxide** is a **strong base**, which can be identified by turning **red litmus paper blue** or turning **phenolphthalein** indicator **pink**.
 
• **Year of Discovery:** Sodium was first isolated in **1807** by **Sir Humphry Davy** through the **electrolysis** of caustic soda.

questions.question: When salt solution is applied to boiled Rhoeo leaf peels, it fails to show plasmolysis due to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**dead cells cannot osmoregulate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plasmolysis** is a biological process that occurs in **living plant cells** when they are placed in a **hypertonic solution** (a solution with a higher solute concentration than the cell sap). During this process, water moves out of the cell through **osmosis**, causing the **protoplasm** to shrink away from the **cell wall**.
 
• When **Rhoeo leaf peels** are **boiled**, the high temperature causes the **denaturation of proteins** and destroys the **plasma membrane**. Boiling effectively **kills the cells**, leading to the loss of their **selective permeability**.
 
• The process of **osmosis** and **osmoregulation** requires a **functional, living semi-permeable membrane**. Since boiling renders the cells **dead**, the membrane can no longer regulate the movement of water or solutes. ***Hence, the statement that dead cells cannot osmoregulate is correct.***
 
• In **dead cells**, the physical and chemical barriers that facilitate **exosmosis** are compromised. Therefore, even when a concentrated **salt solution** is applied, the characteristic shrinkage of the **cytoplasm** (plasmolysis) is not observed because the biological machinery required for **osmotic movement** is non-functional.
 
• The **cell wall** of a plant cell is **fully permeable** to water and dissolved substances; it is the **plasma membrane** that acts as the regulatory barrier. In boiled leaves, the **plasma membrane** is ruptured, allowing substances to move freely without **osmotic control**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rhoeo discolor (Tradescantia spathacea):**

 
 
• This plant is widely used in **botany experiments** because its lower **epidermal cells** contain **anthocyanin**, a **purple-colored pigment** located in the **vacuoles**.
 
• The presence of this pigment makes the **protoplast** easily visible under a **microscope**, allowing students to clearly observe the stages of **plasmolysis** and **deplasmolysis**.
 
 
 
• **Stages of Plasmolysis:**
 
 
• **Limiting Plasmolysis:** The initial stage where the **osmotic pressure** of the cell equals the external solution, and the **turgor pressure** becomes **zero**.
 
• **Incipient Plasmolysis:** The stage where the **protoplast** begins to pull away from the **cell wall** at the corners.
 
• **Evident Plasmolysis:** The final stage where the **cytoplasm** is completely detached from the **cell wall** and assumes a spherical or irregular shape in the center.
 
 
 
• **Deplasmolysis:**
 
 
• If a **plasmolyzed cell** is placed in a **hypotonic solution** (like **distilled water**), water enters the cell through **endosmosis**.
 
• The **protoplast** swells and returns to its original position against the **cell wall**. Like plasmolysis, this process can only occur in **living cells**.
 
 
 
• **Turgor Pressure:**
 
 
• In a **hypotonic environment**, water enters the plant cell, creating **turgor pressure** against the rigid **cell wall**. This pressure is essential for maintaining the **structural integrity** and upright posture of **non-woody plants**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Permeability:** It is important to distinguish that the **cell wall** is **completely permeable** (allows everything to pass), whereas the **plasma membrane** is **selectively permeable** (allows only specific molecules like water to pass freely).
 
• **Osmoregulation in Plants:** It is the mechanism by which plants maintain the **water potential** and **solute concentration** within their cells. This is a **metabolic process** that ceases immediately upon the **death of the cell**.
 
• **Hypertonic vs. Hypotonic:** A **hypertonic solution** has a **lower water potential** than the cell, leading to **water loss**, while a **hypotonic solution** has a **higher water potential**, leading to **water gain**.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct for concave mirrors?

options.text: They are used as rear-view mirrors.
They are used by dentists to see enlarged images of teeth.

questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**They are used by dentists to see enlarged images of teeth**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Concave mirrors** are widely used by **dentists** to see large images of the teeth of patients. When the tooth is placed between the **focus (F)** and the **pole (P)** of the mirror, it produces an **enlarged**, **virtual**, and **upright** image. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Rear-view mirrors** in vehicles are generally **convex mirrors** because they give an **erect**, though diminished, image and provide a **wider field of view** to the driver. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Concave mirrors** are capable of producing **magnified images**. For example, when an object is placed between the **center of curvature (C)** and the **principal focus (F)**, the resulting image is **magnified** and **real**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• A **concave mirror** does not always produce **virtual images**; in fact, it produces **real and inverted images** for most positions of the object (at infinity, beyond C, at C, and between C and F). It only produces a **virtual image** when the object is placed between the **focus** and the **mirror**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is They are used by dentists to see enlarged images of teeth.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition and Nature:**

 
 
• A **concave mirror** is a **spherical mirror** whose reflecting surface is curved **inwards**, facing the center of the sphere. It is also known as a **converging mirror** because it converges light rays that strike its surface.
 
• The **focal length** of a concave mirror is considered **negative** according to the **Cartesian sign convention**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• **Shaving Mirrors:** They are used to see a **larger image** of the face for a better shave.
 
• **Torches and Headlights:** Concave mirrors are used in **search-lights** and **vehicle headlights** to get **powerful parallel beams** of light by placing the bulb at the **focus**.
 
• **Solar Furnaces:** Large concave mirrors are used to **concentrate sunlight** to produce heat in solar furnaces.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation Characteristics:**
 
 
• The **nature, position, and size** of the image formed by a concave mirror depend on the distance of the object from the **pole**.
 
• If the object is at the **Center of Curvature (C)**, the image is **real, inverted, and the same size** as the object.
 
• If the object is at **infinity**, the image is formed at the **focus (F)** and is **highly diminished**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Convex Mirrors:**

 
 
• Unlike concave mirrors, **convex mirrors** (diverging mirrors) always produce **virtual, erect, and diminished images** regardless of the object's distance.
 
• This property makes **convex mirrors** ideal for **blind turns** on roads and **shop security** mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula and Magnification:**
 
 
• The **Mirror Formula** is given by **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**, where **f** is focal length, **v** is image distance, and **u** is object distance.
 
• **Linear Magnification (m)** is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, also expressed as **m = -v/u**. For a **concave mirror**, magnification can be **less than 1, equal to 1, or greater than 1**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about variations is INCORRECT?

options.text: Variation makes species prone to extinction.
Variation enables adaptation to changing environments.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Variation makes species prone to extinction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Variation** refers to the differences in **DNA sequences** and physical traits among individuals within a population or species. These differences are the primary drivers of **evolution** and **biodiversity**.
 
• Variation ensures species survival during disasters: In a changing environment or during natural calamities, individuals with specific variations may have a better chance of survival compared to others. For example, in a bacterial population, some might be resistant to heat; during a sudden **temperature increase**, only these variants survive. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Variation makes species prone to extinction: This is **incorrect**. In reality, a lack of variation (genetic uniformity) makes a species more vulnerable to extinction. Higher **genetic diversity** provides a "buffer" against environmental changes, whereas low variation means the entire population could be wiped out by a single event. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Variation enables adaptation to changing environments: Through the process of **Natural Selection**, favorable variations that help an organism survive and reproduce in its current environment are passed on to the next generation. This is the basis of **adaptation**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Provides resilience against diseases: Genetic variation ensures that not all individuals are equally susceptible to the same **pathogens**. If a new **virus** or **bacteria** attacks a population, some individuals may possess a natural **immunity** due to their unique genetic makeup. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the incorrect statement (and thus the correct answer) is "Variation makes species prone to extinction".***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sources of Variation:**

 
 
• **Mutation:** A random change in the **DNA sequence** which can create new alleles.
 
• **Recombination:** During **Meiosis** (cell division), genes are shuffled between chromosomes, leading to new combinations of traits in offspring.
 
• **Sexual Reproduction:** The combining of genetic material from two different parents significantly increases the **genetic pool** of the population.
 
 
 
• **Importance in Evolution:**
 
 
• **Charles Darwin**, in his book "**On the Origin of Species**" (**1859**), highlighted that variation is the raw material upon which natural selection acts.
 
• Without variation, there would be no **speciation** (the formation of new and distinct species).
 
 
 
• **Types of Variation:**
 
 
• **Continuous Variation:** Traits like **height** or **skin color** that show a range of small differences.
 
• **Discontinuous Variation:** Traits like **blood groups** or the ability to roll the tongue, which fall into distinct categories with no intermediates.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **DNA Copying:** Variation often arises during **DNA replication** before cell division. While the process is highly accurate, occasional "errors" or biochemical inaccuracies occur, leading to variations in the progeny.
 
• **Survival of the Fittest:** This concept, coined by **Herbert Spencer** and utilized by **Darwin**, explains that individuals with the most useful variations for their specific environment are the ones most likely to survive and **reproduce**.
 
• **Environmental Factors:** While many variations are **heritable** (passed via genes), some are **acquired** during an organism's lifetime due to environmental influences (e.g., muscle building or scarring) and are generally not passed to the next generation.
 
• **Population Stability:** Variation helps maintain the stability of an **ecosystem**. A diverse range of species and genetic traits within those species ensures that the ecosystem can recover from stresses such as **climate change** or **habitat loss**.

questions.question: Which event does NOT directly occur during photosynthesis in green plants?

options.text: Reduction of carbon dioxide to carbohydrates
Conversion of light energy into chemical energy
Absorption of light energy by chlorophyll
Breakdown of carbohydrates to release energy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Breakdown of carbohydrates to release energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Photosynthesis** is a complex **anabolic process** by which **green plants** and certain other organisms transform **light energy** into **chemical energy**.
 
• **Absorption of light energy by chlorophyll**: This is the primary step where **chlorophyll pigments**, located in the **chloroplasts**, capture photons from sunlight. ***Hence, statement 3 is a direct event that occurs during photosynthesis.***
 
• **Conversion of light energy into chemical energy**: During the **light-dependent phase**, absorbed solar energy is converted into **ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate) and **NADPH**. This phase also involves the **photolysis of water**, where water molecules are split into **hydrogen** and **oxygen**. ***Hence, statement 2 is a direct event that occurs during photosynthesis.***
 
• **Reduction of carbon dioxide to carbohydrates**: This occurs during the **Calvin Cycle** (light-independent reaction) in the **stroma** of the chloroplast. The energy from **ATP** and **NADPH** is used to fix **CO2** into **glucose**. ***Hence, statement 1 is a direct event that occurs during photosynthesis.***
 
• **Breakdown of carbohydrates to release energy**: This process is known as **cellular respiration**. It is a **catabolic process** that takes place in the **mitochondria** to provide energy for the cell's metabolic activities. While plants do respire, this specific action is the functional opposite of photosynthesis. ***Hence, statement 4 does NOT occur during the process of photosynthesis.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Site of Photosynthesis**:

 
 
• Photosynthesis takes place in specialized organelles called **chloroplasts**. These organelles contain a green pigment called **chlorophyll**.
 
• The **grana** (stacks of thylakoids) are the site for **light reactions**, where light is trapped.
 
• The **stroma** is the site for **dark reactions**, where the chemical synthesis of **carbohydrates** occurs.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Equation**:
 
 
• The overall reaction is represented as: **6CO2 + 6H2O + Light Energy → C6H12O6 + 6O2**.
 
• This equation shows that **carbon dioxide** and **water** are the raw materials used to produce **glucose** and **oxygen** as a byproduct.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing Photosynthesis**:
 
 
• **Light Intensity**: Increased light typically increases the rate of photosynthesis until a saturation point is reached.
 
• **Carbon Dioxide Concentration**: As a primary reactant, higher **CO2** levels can increase the rate of **sugar** production.
 
• **Temperature**: Since the process involves enzymes (like **RuBisCO**), it is sensitive to temperature changes, with an **optimum range** usually between **25°C to 35°C**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Autotrophs**: Green plants are considered **autotrophs** because they can synthesize their own food using inorganic substances and **solar energy**.
 
• **Stomata**: These are tiny pores found mainly on the **epidermis** of leaves. They facilitate the exchange of gases, allowing **CO2** to enter and **O2** to exit the plant body.
 
• **Product Storage**: The **glucose** produced during photosynthesis is often converted into **starch** for long-term storage in different parts of the plant, such as roots, tubers, and seeds.
 
• **Energy Currency**: While **ATP** is produced during the light reaction of photosynthesis, it is immediately consumed in the dark reaction to build **carbohydrates**. The **ATP** used for general cellular work in plants is actually generated through **respiration**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic reaction of saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Substitution reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saturated hydrocarbons**, also known as **alkanes**, are organic compounds consisting entirely of **single covalent bonds** between carbon atoms. Their general chemical formula is **CnH2n+2**.
 
• Because all the valencies of carbon atoms are fully satisfied by single bonds, alkanes are relatively **unreactive** under normal conditions. They do not have double or triple bonds to "open up" for new atoms.
 
• The characteristic reaction of alkanes is the **Substitution reaction**. In this process, one or more **hydrogen atoms** of the hydrocarbon are replaced by other atoms or groups of atoms, such as **halogens**. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
• A classic example is the **chlorination of methane**. In the presence of **ultraviolet (UV) light** or **diffused sunlight**, a chlorine atom replaces a hydrogen atom in **Methane (CH4)** to form **Chloromethane (CH3Cl)** and **Hydrogen Chloride (HCl)**.
 
• This reaction can continue until all the hydrogen atoms in the alkane are substituted. For methane, the sequence ends with **Tetrachloromethane (CCl4)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Addition Reaction:**

 
 
• This reaction is characteristic of **unsaturated hydrocarbons** like **alkenes** (double bonds) and **alkynes** (triple bonds).
 
• In an addition reaction, molecules like **Hydrogen (H2)** or **Bromine (Br2)** are added across the multiple bonds to turn them into saturated compounds. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect for alkanes.***
 
 
 
• **Neutralisation:**
 
 
• This is a chemical reaction between an **acid** and a **base** to produce **salt** and **water**.
 
• Hydrocarbons are generally **neutral** and do not participate in standard acid-base neutralisation. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Polymerisation:**
 
 
• This involves the combination of many small molecules called **monomers** to form a large molecule called a **polymer**.
 
• While **unsaturated** hydrocarbons like **ethene** undergo polymerisation to form **polyethene**, saturated alkanes do not typically exhibit this as a characteristic reaction. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Combustion:**
 
 
• Alkanes react readily with **Oxygen (O2)** upon heating. **Complete combustion** produces **Carbon dioxide (CO2)**, **Water (H2O)**, and a large amount of **heat and light**, making them excellent **fuels**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Paraffins:** Alkanes were traditionally called **paraffins** (from Latin **parum** = little, **affinis** = affinity), highlighting their low chemical reactivity toward common reagents like acids, bases, or oxidising agents at **room temperature**.
 
• **Homologous Series:** Alkanes form a series where each member differs from the next by a **-CH2-** unit and has a mass difference of **14 units**.
 
• **Isomerism:** Alkanes with **four or more** carbon atoms (starting from **Butane**) can show **structural isomerism**, where they have the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms.
 
• **Physical State:** At room temperature, the first four alkanes (**Methane, Ethane, Propane, and Butane**) are **gases**, while those from **C5 to C17** are **liquids**, and higher alkanes are **solids**.

questions.question: What is a decomposition reaction?

options.text: A compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances
Two or more substances combine to form one product
A single substance is formed from two or more reactants

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Decomposition reaction** is a fundamental type of chemical process where a **single reactant** breaks down into **two or more simpler products**. This is the exact definition provided in the first option. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• In these reactions, the **chemical bonds** in the reactant molecule are broken, requiring an input of energy. The general chemical equation for this process can be represented as **AB → A + B**.
 
• Statement 2 describes a **Double Displacement reaction**, where **two compounds exchange ions** to form two new compounds, often resulting in a precipitate or water. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 3 and Statement 4 describe a **Combination reaction** (also known as a synthesis reaction), where **two or more substances combine** to form a **single product**. This is the opposite of decomposition. ***Hence, statement 3 and 4 are incorrect.***
 
• A classic example of decomposition is the **thermal decomposition of Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3)**, which, when heated, yields **Calcium Oxide (CaO)** and **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Decomposition Reactions:**

 
 
• **Thermal Decomposition:** This occurs when **heat energy** is used to break down a substance. For instance, heating **Lead Nitrate** crystals leads to the emission of **brown fumes of Nitrogen Dioxide** and the formation of Lead Oxide.
 
• **Electrolytic Decomposition (Electrolysis):** This process uses **electrical energy** to drive the decomposition. A primary **example** is the **electrolysis of water**, where water (H2O) decomposes into **Hydrogen gas** and **Oxygen gas** when an electric current is passed through it.
 
• **Photolytic Decomposition (Photolysis):** This breakdown is triggered by **light energy (photons)**. For example, **Silver Chloride (AgCl)** turns **grey** in sunlight because it decomposes into **Silver metal** and **Chlorine gas**.
 
 
 
• **Combination Reactions:**
 
 
• These are reactions where a **single substance** is formed from multiple reactants. A common **example** is the **burning of magnesium ribbon** in air to form **Magnesium Oxide** or the **burning of coal** (Carbon + Oxygen → Carbon Dioxide).
 
 
 
• **Double Displacement Reactions:**
 
 
• These involve the **exchange of ions** between reactants. A well-known **example** is the reaction between **Sodium Sulphate** and **Barium Chloride**, which produces a **white precipitate** of **Barium Sulphate** and Sodium Chloride.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Energy Nature:** Most decomposition reactions are **endothermic** in nature because they involve the **absorption of energy** (heat, light, or electricity) to break existing chemical bonds.
 
• **Biological Application:** Decomposition reactions are vital in the **human body**. During **digestion**, complex food molecules like **starch** and **proteins** undergo decomposition reactions to break down into simpler substances like **glucose** and **amino acids**, which the body can then absorb.
 
• **Industrial Use:** Decomposition of **Calcium Carbonate** is a key step in the **manufacturing of cement**. The **Calcium Oxide (Quick Lime)** produced is a vital raw material in various industries.
 
• **Photography:** The **photolytic decomposition** of **Silver Bromide (AgBr)** was traditionally used in **Black and White Photography** to capture images on film.

questions.question: A retarding force of 10 N acts on a body. The work done due to this force is -200 J. What will be the magnitude and direction of the displacement of the body under the action of this force?

options.text: 20 m; opposite to the direction of the force
2000 m; in the same direction as the force
2000 m; opposite to the direction of the force
20 m; in the same direction as the force

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 m; opposite to the direction of the force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Work Done** is defined as the product of the **magnitude of the force** acting on a body and the **displacement** caused by that force in the direction of the force. The formula is **W = F × d × cos(θ)**, where **θ** is the angle between the force and displacement.
 
• A **retarding force** is a force that acts in the **opposite direction** to the motion (displacement) of an object, such as friction or brakes applied to a vehicle. Because the force and displacement are in opposite directions, the angle **θ** is **180 degrees**.
 
• In this problem, the **force (F)** is 10 N

questions.question: If the radius of curvature of a convex mirror used for rear-view on an automobile is 4.00 m, what is its focal length?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between the **focal length (f)** and the **radius of curvature (R)** of a spherical mirror (both convex and concave) is given by the formula **f = R / 2**.
 
• In this specific problem, the **radius of curvature (R)** of the **convex mirror** is given as **4.00 m**.
 
• By substituting the value into the formula: **f = 4.00 m / 2 = 2.00 m**. ***Hence, the focal length of the mirror is 2 m.***
 
• For a **convex mirror**, the **principal focus (F)** and the **center of curvature (C)** lie behind the mirror; therefore, according to the **sign convention**, the focal length is taken as **positive**.
 
• The **principal focus** of a spherical mirror is a point on the **principal axis** where light rays traveling parallel to the axis appear to diverge from (in the case of a convex mirror) or actually meet (in the case of a concave mirror).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convex Mirror Characteristics:**

 
 
• A **convex mirror** is also known as a **diverging mirror** because it reflects parallel light rays away from each other.
 
• It always forms a **virtual**, **erect**, and **diminished** (smaller than the object) image, regardless of the distance of the object from the mirror.
 
• The **focal length** of a convex mirror is always **positive** according to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**.
 
 
 
• **Uses in Automobiles:**
 
 
• **Convex mirrors** are preferred as **rear-view mirrors** in vehicles because they provide a much wider **field of view** compared to plane mirrors.
 
• Since the images formed are **diminished**, they allow the driver to see a larger area of traffic behind the vehicle.
 
• The fact that the image is always **erect** (upright) is critical for safety while driving.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• A **concave mirror** (converging mirror) has a **negative focal length** because its focus is in front of the reflecting surface.
 
• Unlike convex mirrors, **concave mirrors** can produce both **real** and **virtual** images depending on the object's position.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **New Cartesian Sign Convention:**

 
 
• The **pole (P)** of the mirror is taken as the **origin**.
 
• Objects are always placed to the **left** of the mirror, meaning light travels from left to right.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of incident light (to the **right** of the pole) are **positive**.
 
• Distances measured against the direction of incident light (to the **left** of the pole) are **negative**.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula and Magnification:**
 
 
• The relationship between object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) is **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**.
 
• **Magnification (m)** is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, expressed as **m = h'/h = -v/u**.
 
• For a **convex mirror**, the magnification **m** is always **less than 1** and **positive**.
 
 
 
• **Center of Curvature (C):** This is the center of the hollow glass sphere of which the mirror is a part. The distance **PC** is the **radius of curvature (R)**, which is exactly **twice** the **focal length**.

questions.question: Which of the following ensures that the DNA amount is NOT doubled in every generation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduction of DNA in gametes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process that ensures the **DNA** amount does not double in every generation is the **reduction of DNA in gametes**, which occurs through a specialized cell division called **meiosis**.
 
• In **sexually reproducing organisms**, the body cells (somatic cells) are typically **diploid**, meaning they contain **two sets** of **chromosomes** (one from each parent).
 
• During the formation of **gametes** (sperm and egg), **meiosis** reduces the **chromosome number** by half, resulting in **haploid** cells that contain only **one set** of **DNA**.
 
• When **fertilization** occurs, the **male gamete** and **female gamete** fuse to form a **zygote**, thereby restoring the original **diploid** (**2n**) number of **chromosomes** characteristic of the species.
 
• Without this **reduction division**, the **DNA** content would double with every successive generation, leading to **polyploidy** and biological instability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meiosis vs. Mitosis:**

 
 
• **Mitosis** is the process of **somatic cell division** where the **DNA** amount remains constant, producing **two identical daughter cells**. It is used for **growth** and **repair**.
 
• **Meiosis** involves **two rounds** of division (**Meiosis I** and **Meiosis II**) but only **one round** of **DNA replication**, which is how the **reduction** is achieved.
 
 
 
• **DNA and Chromosomes:**
 
 
• **DNA** (Deoxyribonucleic acid) is the **hereditary material** located in the **nucleus**. In **humans**, the **diploid** number is **46 chromosomes** (**23 pairs**), while the **haploid** gametes contain **23 chromosomes**.
 
• The concept of **germ plasm** and the necessity of **reduction division** was notably proposed by **August Weismann** in **1887**.
 
 
 
• **Biological Significance:**
 
 
• Beyond maintaining **ploidy**, **meiosis** facilitates **genetic variation** through **crossing over** during **prophase I**, where **homologous chromosomes** exchange **genetic material**.
 
• **Fertilization** (or **syngamy**) is the crucial counterpart to **meiosis** that ensures the **continuity** of the species with a stable **genome** size across **generations**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Context:**
 
 
• **Division of neurons**: Neurons are **post-mitotic** cells in adults, meaning they generally do not divide, and their division would not affect **DNA** inheritance across **generations**.
 
• **Division of body cells**: Also known as **mitosis**, this maintains the **DNA** amount within an individual but does not handle the **generational** transfer of **DNA**.
 
• **Consistency of DNA in gametes**: While **DNA** must be consistent in terms of **quality**, if the **quantity** remained the same as **somatic cells**, the **DNA** would double upon **fusion**.

• In a **Diamond**, each carbon atom is connected to **four other carbon atoms** by strong **covalent bonds**, forming a rigid **three-dimensional tetrahedral structure**. This structure accounts for its extreme **hardness** and **durability**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Allotropy**:

 
 
• It is the property of some chemical elements to exist in **two or more different forms**, in the same physical state, known as **allotropes** of the elements.
 
• Allotropes typically exhibit different **physical properties** (like hardness and conductivity) but identical **chemical properties**.
 
 
 
• **Other Allotropes of Carbon**:
 
 
• **Graphite**: Carbon atoms are arranged in **hexagonal layers**. It is **soft, slippery**, and used as a **lubricant** and in **pencil leads**. It is a **good conductor of electricity** due to delocalized electrons.
 
• **Fullerenes**: Discovered in **1985**, these are molecules composed entirely of carbon in the form of a **hollow sphere**, ellipsoid, or tube. **Buckminsterfullerene (C60)** is the most common form, resembling a **soccer ball**.

• **Natural Formation**: Natural diamonds are formed at **high temperatures and pressures** at depths of **150 to 200 kilometers** within the Earth's **mantle**.
 
• **Chemical Symbolism**: Carbon has the atomic number **6** and belongs to **Group 14** of the periodic table. It displays **tetravalency** and **catenation**, which allows it to form a vast variety of compounds and structures.
 
• **Measurement**: The weight of a diamond is measured in **carats**. One **carat** is equal to **200 milligrams**.

__
 
• **Judicious energy use** involves the **efficient** and **responsible** consumption of **electricity** and other resources to minimize waste and reduce the **environmental impact**.
 
• **Using bulbs or fluorescent tubes** for illumination is a standard and necessary practice; however, choosing **Fluorescent tubes** or **CFLs** over traditional **incandescent bulbs** is a mark of **energy efficiency** as they consume significantly less **wattage** for the same amount of light. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

questions.question: The process by which the developing embryo gets associated with the lining of the uterus is called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**implantation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Implantation** is defined as the process by which the developing **embryo** (at the **blastocyst** stage) attaches itself to the **endometrium**, which is the internal lining of the **uterus**.
 
• This critical biological event typically occurs **6 to 12 days** after **fertilisation** has taken place in the **fallopian tube**.
 
• During this process, the outer layer of the blastocyst, known as the **trophoblast**, secretes enzymes that allow it to penetrate the **uterine wall**, establishing a connection for nutrient exchange between the mother and the developing **embryo**.
 
• Once **implantation** is successful, the **embryo** begins to receive oxygen and nutrients from the mother's blood, and the production of **human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG)** starts, which is the hormone detected in **pregnancy tests**. ***Hence, the correct answer is implantation.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fertilisation**:

 
 
• This is the process of fusion of a male gamete (**sperm**) with a female gamete (**ovum**) to form a **diploid zygote**.
 
• In humans, **fertilisation** usually occurs in the **ampullary-isthmic junction** of the **fallopian tube**.
 
 
 
• **Embryogenesis**:
 
 
• It is the process by which the **embryo** forms and develops. It starts with the **fertilisation** of the ovum and continues through the stages of **cleavage**, **blastulation**, **gastrulation**, and **organogenesis**.
 
• During **embryogenesis**, the single-celled **zygote** transforms into a multi-cellular complex organism.
 
 
 
• **Abortion**:
 
 
• This refers to the termination of a **pregnancy** by the removal or expulsion of an **embryo** or **fetus** before it can survive outside the **uterus**.
 
• It can occur spontaneously (commonly called a **miscarriage**) or can be purposely induced through **medical** or **surgical** means.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Blastocyst Stage**: The **embryo** reaches the **uterus** about **3 to 4 days** after **fertilisation** and floats in the uterine cavity for another **2 to 3 days** before **implantation** begins.
 
• **Endometrium Role**: The **hormone progesterone**, secreted by the **corpus luteum**, is essential for maintaining the **endometrium** in a receptive state for **implantation**.
 
• **Ectopic Pregnancy**: If **implantation** occurs outside the **uterus**, most commonly in the **fallopian tubes**, it is called an **ectopic pregnancy**, which is a medical emergency.
 
• **Placenta Formation**: Following **implantation**, the **trophoblast** cells and the **uterine tissue** together form the **placenta**, a structural and functional unit between the **developing fetus** and the **maternal body**.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines the concentration of a solution?

options.text: The amount of solute present in a given amount of solution
The amount of solution present in a given amount of solute
The amount of solvent present in a given amount of solution
The amount of solvent present in a given amount of solute

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The amount of solute present in a given amount of solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **concentration** of a solution refers to the **amount of solute** dissolved in a particular **amount (mass or volume)** of the **solution** or **solvent**.
 
• It is a quantitative measure that helps determine how "strong" or "weak" a solution is based on the proportion of its components.
 
• **Statement 1**: This statement correctly defines concentration as the ratio of the **solute** to the total **solution**. This is the standard way to express concentration in chemistry. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 2**: This statement suggests that concentration is the amount of solution in a solute, which is logically incorrect as the **solute** is a component of the **solution**, not vice versa. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 3**: This statement describes the amount of **solvent** in a solution; while this indicates the degree of **dilution**, the term "concentration" specifically tracks the **solute**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4**: This statement defines the amount of solvent in a given amount of solute, which is essentially the inverse of the solubility relationship and does not represent the definition of concentration. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Common mathematical expressions for concentration include **Mass by mass percentage**, **Mass by volume percentage**, and **Molarity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Solute and Solvent:**

 
 
• The **Solute** is the substance that is **dissolved** in another substance (usually present in a **smaller quantity**), such as **salt** or **sugar**.
 
• The **Solvent** is the substance in which the solute is dissolved (usually present in a **larger quantity**), such as **water** or **alcohol**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Solutions based on Concentration:**
 
 
• **Dilute Solution**: A solution containing a very **small amount of solute** relative to the amount of solvent.
 
• **Concentrated Solution**: A solution containing a **large amount of solute** dissolved in the solvent.
 
• **Saturated Solution**: A solution in which **no more solute** can be dissolved at a specific **temperature**.
 
• **Unsaturated Solution**: A solution where the amount of solute is **less than** the **saturation level**, meaning more can still be dissolved.
 
 
 
• **Solubility:**
 
 
• The **maximum amount of solute** that can be dissolved in **100 grams** of solvent at a specific **temperature** is known as its **solubility**.
 
• Factors such as **temperature** and **pressure** can significantly affect the solubility of solids and gases in liquids.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mass by Mass Percentage of a solution**: Calculated as (**Mass of solute** / **Mass of solution**) × **100**.
 
• **Mass by Volume Percentage of a solution**: Calculated as (**Mass of solute** / **Volume of solution**) × **100**.
 
• **Molarity (M)**: It is defined as the **number of moles of solute** dissolved in **1 liter** of solution. It is the most commonly used unit of concentration in laboratories.
 
• **Molality (m)**: It is defined as the **moles of solute** per **kilogram of solvent**. Unlike molarity, molality does not change with **temperature** changes because mass is constant.
 
• **Parts Per Million (ppm)**: Used for expressing very **low concentrations**, such as the amount of **pollutants** in the **atmosphere** or **water**.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs represent the Isobar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**40K19 and 40Ar18**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isobars** are defined as atoms of different chemical elements that have the same **mass number (A)** but different **atomic numbers (Z)**.
 
• In the pair **40K19** and **40Ar18**, both species possess a **mass number** of **40**. However, **Potassium (K)** has an **atomic number** of **19**, while **Argon (Ar)** has an **atomic number** of **18**. ***Hence, this pair represents Isobars and is the correct answer.***
 
• The **mass number** is the total count of **protons** and **neutrons** in the nucleus. For **40K19**, there are **19 protons** and **21 neutrons** (40 - 19 = 21). For **40Ar18**, there are **18 protons** and **22 neutrons** (40 - 18 = 22).
 
• Because **Isobars** have different **atomic numbers**, they have different numbers of **electrons** and thus exhibit completely different **chemical properties** and occupy different positions in the **Modern Periodic Table**.
 
• Other examples of **Isobars** include **Carbon-14 (14C6)** and **Nitrogen-14 (14N7)**, where both have a **mass number** of **14** but different **atomic numbers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Isotopes**:

 
 
• These are atoms of the same element that have the same **atomic number** but different **mass numbers**.
 
• Example: **15O8** and **16O8** are isotopes of **Oxygen**. Similarly, **235U92** and **238U92** are isotopes of **Uranium**. ***Hence, options 2 and 4 are incorrect.***
 
• Isotopes have the same **chemical properties** because they have the same number of **electrons**.
 
 
 
• **Isotones**:
 
 
• These are atoms of different elements that have the same number of **neutrons**.
 
• In the pair **15N7** and **16O8**, **Nitrogen** has **8 neutrons** (15 - 7 = 8) and **Oxygen** also has **8 neutrons** (16 - 8 = 8). ***Hence, option 3 represents isotones and is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Atomic Number (Z)**: This value represents the number of **protons** present in the nucleus of an atom. It defines the identity of the **element**.
 
• **Mass Number (A)**: This represents the sum of the number of **protons** and **neutrons** (collectively called **nucleons**) in the nucleus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **Isobar** was originally suggested by **Alfred Walter Stewart** in the year **1918**. It is derived from the Greek words 'isos' meaning **equal** and 'baros' meaning **weight**.
 
• While **Isobars** have different **chemical properties**, they may have similar **physical properties** that depend on the **mass**, such as **density** (though they are still distinct due to different atomic structures).
 
• **Potassium-40** is a significant radioactive isotope used in **geochronology** (Potassium-Argon dating) to determine the **age** of ancient **rocks** and **minerals**.
 
• In **nuclear physics**, isobars are important for studying **beta decay**, where a nucleus transforms into its isobar by changing a **neutron** into a **proton** (or vice versa) to reach a more **stable** state.

Select the option that is true regarding the following two statements labelled Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

**Assertion (A): **Insulin helps lower blood glucose levels.

**Reason (R):** Insulin converts glucose into glycogen for storage in the liver.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A)** states that **Insulin** helps lower **blood glucose levels**. **Insulin** is an essential **hormone** produced by the **pancreas** that allows your body to use **sugar (glucose)** from carbohydrates in the food that you eat for energy or to store glucose for future use. ***Hence, Assertion (A) is correct.***
 
• **Reason (R)** explains that **Insulin** converts **glucose** into **glycogen** for storage in the **liver**. When **blood glucose levels** are high, the **pancreas** secretes **insulin**, which signals the **liver**, **muscles**, and **fat cells** to take up the **glucose** from the blood. In the **liver** and **muscles**, this **glucose** is converted into **glycogen** through a process called **glycogenesis**. ***Hence, Reason (R) is correct.***
 
• The primary mechanism by which **insulin** lowers the concentration of **glucose** in the **bloodstream** is by facilitating its uptake into cells and its conversion into **storage forms** like **glycogen**.
 
• Since the conversion and storage of **glucose** as **glycogen** directly results in the reduction of circulating **blood sugar**, the **Reason (R)** serves as a scientifically accurate explanation for the **Assertion (A)**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Pancreas and Insulin Secretion:**

 
 
• The **pancreas** contains clusters of cells known as the **Islets of Langerhans**.
 
• **Beta cells** within these clusters are responsible for the synthesis and secretion of **insulin**.
 
• **Insulin** is considered an **anabolic hormone** because it promotes the storage of **glucose**, **amino acids**, and **fats**.
 
 
 
• **Glucagon - The Antagonist:**
 
 
• While **insulin** lowers blood sugar, another hormone called **glucagon** (secreted by **Alpha cells** of the **pancreas**) raises it.
 
• **Glucagon** triggers **glycogenolysis**, which is the breakdown of **glycogen** back into **glucose** when **blood sugar** is low.
 
 
 
• **Diabetes Mellitus:**
 
 
• A deficiency in **insulin** production or a decrease in the body's responsiveness to it leads to **Diabetes Mellitus**.
 
• **Type 1 Diabetes** occurs when the **pancreas** produces little or no **insulin**.
 
• **Type 2 Diabetes** occurs when the body's cells become resistant to **insulin**, leading to **hyperglycemia** (high blood sugar).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Homeostasis:** The balance between **insulin** and **glucagon** ensures **glucose homeostasis**, maintaining **blood sugar** within a narrow range (typically **70-100 mg/dL** during fasting).
 
• **Discovery:** **Insulin** was first isolated in **1921** by **Sir Frederick G. Banting** and **Charles H. Best** at the **University of Toronto**.
 
• **Target Tissues:** Beyond the **liver**, **insulin** significantly affects **skeletal muscle** (where it also stores **glycogen**) and **adipose tissue** (where it promotes the storage of **lipids**).
 
• **Glycogenesis vs Glycogenolysis:** **Glycogenesis** is the formation of **glycogen** from **glucose** (stimulated by **insulin**), whereas **glycogenolysis** is the breakdown of **glycogen** into **glucose** (stimulated by **glucagon** or **epinephrine**).

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about resistivity?

options.text: It is a property of the material.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It depends on the length of the wire**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resistivity** is a fundamental and **intrinsic property** of a material that quantifies how strongly it opposes the flow of electric current. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• It is mathematically defined as the **resistance** of a conductor having a **unit length** and a **unit area of cross-section**. While **resistance** changes with dimensions, **resistivity** remains constant for a specific material at a given **temperature**.
 
• The **resistivity** of a material **does not depend** on its **geometrical dimensions** such as **length** or **thickness (area)**. It only depends on the **nature of the material** and its **temperature**. *Hence, statement 3 is NOT correct.*
 
• The **resistivity** of metallic conductors typically **increases with an increase in temperature** because the thermal vibrations of atoms interfere with the flow of electrons. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• The **SI unit** of **resistivity** is the **ohm-meter** (written as **Ω ⋅ m**). This unit is derived from the formula for resistance **R = ρ (L/A)**, where **ρ** is resistivity. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Difference between Resistance and Resistivity:**

 
 
• **Resistance** (R) is the property of a specific **object** or component and depends on its **length**, **area**, and **material**. Its unit is the **Ohm** (Ω).
 
• **Resistivity** (ρ) is the property of the **substance** itself. For example, a **1-meter copper wire** and a **10-meter copper wire** will have different **resistances** but the **same resistivity**.
 
 
 
• **Classification of Materials:**
 
 
• **Conductors:** Materials like **Silver** and **Copper** have very **low resistivity**, in the range of **10^-8 Ω⋅m** to **10^-6 Ω⋅m**. **Silver** is the best conductor with a resistivity of approximately **1.59 × 10^-8 Ω⋅m** at **20°C**.
 
• **Insulators:** Materials like **Glass**, **Rubber**, and **Ebonite** have very **high resistivity**, ranging from **10^12 Ω⋅m** to **10^17 Ω⋅m**.
 
• **Alloys:** Substances like **Nichrome** and **Constantan** have higher resistivity than their constituent metals and are used in **heating elements** because they do not **oxidize (burn)** easily at high temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Conductivity:**
 
 
• The **reciprocal of resistivity** is known as **electrical conductivity** (σ). It measures how easily a material allows current to flow. Its **SI unit** is **siemens per meter** (S/m) or **(ohm-meter)^-1**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance:** Resistance of a uniform conductor is **directly proportional to its length** (L) and **inversely proportional to its area of cross-section** (A).
 
• **Temperature Coefficient:** For most **metals**, the **temperature coefficient of resistivity** is **positive**. However, for **semiconductors** and **insulators**, resistivity typically **decreases** as temperature increases (negative temperature coefficient).
 
• **Usage in Appliances:** The **high resistivity** of alloys like **Manganin** and **Constantan** makes them ideal for making **standard resistors** because their resistivity changes very little with small changes in **temperature**.

questions.question: Which of the following represents corrosion?
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Rusting of iron**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Corrosion** is a natural process that converts a refined metal into a more chemically stable form such as oxide, hydroxide, or sulfide. It is the gradual destruction of materials (usually **metals**) by chemical and/or electrochemical reaction with their environment.
 
• **Rusting of iron** is a specific type of corrosion that occurs when **iron** objects are exposed to **oxygen** and **moisture** (water) for a long time. The reddish-brown flaky substance formed is called **rust** (hydrated iron oxide). ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Burning of LPG** (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) is a **combustion reaction**. While it is a chemical change, it involves the rapid oxidation of fuel to produce heat and light, rather than the slow deterioration of a metal surface. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Boiling of water** is a **physical change** where water transitions from a liquid state to a gaseous state (steam). No new chemical substance is formed during this process. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Dissolving sugar in water** is also a **physical change**. The sugar molecules disperse throughout the water, but their chemical identity remains unchanged, and the sugar can be recovered by evaporating the water. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Rusting of iron.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Nature of Rusting:**

 
 
• The process of **rusting** can be represented by the following equation: **4Fe + 3O2 + 6H2O → 4Fe(OH)3**. The final product eventually dehydrates to form **Fe2O3·nH2O**.
 
• Both **oxygen** and **water** (or moisture) are essential for rusting to occur. In **coastal areas**, rusting is faster because the presence of **salt** in water speeds up the process of oxidation.
 
 
 
• **Prevention of Corrosion:**
 
 
• **Galvanization**: It is the process of depositing a thin layer of **zinc** on **iron** or **steel** to protect it from corrosion. Since **zinc** is more reactive than **iron**, it oxidizes first, protecting the underlying metal.
 
• **Alloying**: Metals are mixed with other elements to enhance their properties. For example, **Stainless steel** is made by mixing **iron** with **carbon**, **chromium**, and **nickel**. It does not rust easily.
 
• **Anodizing**: This involves forming a thick oxide layer of **aluminum** to make it resistant to further corrosion.
 
• **Other Methods**: Painting, **oiling**, **greasing**, or **chrome plating** are common ways to prevent the metal surface from coming into contact with air and moisture.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Corrosion in Other Metals:**

 
 
• **Silver**: It reacts with **sulfur** in the air (from hydrogen sulfide) to form a black coating of **silver sulfide** (Ag2S). This is often called **tarnishing**.
 
• **Copper**: When exposed to moist air, **copper** reacts with **carbon dioxide** and **water** to form a green coating of **basic copper carbonate** [CuCO3·Cu(OH)2].
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• Corrosion causes enormous damage to **car bodies**, **bridges**, **iron railings**, **ships**, and all objects made of metals, especially those made of **iron**.
 
• It is a significant **economic burden** globally, leading to the loss of millions of tons of steel every **year**, necessitating constant replacement and maintenance of infrastructure.

questions.question: If the force on an object is doubled while its mass remains the same, the acceleration:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**also doubles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Newton’s Second Law of Motion**, the **acceleration** of an object is **directly proportional** to the **net force** acting on it and **inversely proportional** to its **mass**.
 
• The relationship is mathematically expressed by the formula **F = ma**, where **F** represents the **resultant force**, **m** represents the **mass** of the object, and **a** represents the **acceleration**.
 
• If the **force** on an object is **doubled** (changed from **F** to **2F**) while the **mass** (**m**) remains **constant**, the **acceleration** must adjust to maintain the equality of the equation.
 
• Using the formula **a = F / m**, the new **acceleration** (**a'**) becomes **a' = (2F) / m**. Since the original **acceleration** was **F / m**, it follows that **a' = 2a**.
 
• This demonstrates that when the **net force** is **multiplied by a factor of two**, the **acceleration** also **multiplied by the same factor**. ***Hence, the correct answer is also doubles.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Second Law of Motion:**

 
 
• This law defines the **quantitative relationship** between **force** and **motion**. It allows for the calculation of how much an object will **speed up** or **slow down** under a specific **load**.
 
• The **SI unit** of **force** is the **Newton (N)**, which is the amount of **force** required to accelerate a **mass** of **1 kilogram (kg)** at a rate of **1 meter per second squared (m/s²)**.
 
• **Acceleration** is a **vector quantity**, which means it has both **magnitude** and **direction**. The **acceleration** always occurs in the **direction** of the **unbalanced force**.
 
 
 
• **Inertia and Mass:**
 
 
• **Mass** is a measure of an object's **inertia**, which is its **resistance** to changes in its **state of motion**.
 
• If the **mass** of an object were to **double** while the **force** remained the same, the **acceleration** would be **halved** because **acceleration** is **inversely proportional** to **mass**.
 
• In **classical mechanics**, **mass** is typically considered **constant** unless the object is traveling at speeds approaching the **speed of light**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sir Isaac Newton** first published these laws of motion in his monumental work, **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica**, in the year **1687**.
 
• **Net Force:** It is important to note that the **force** mentioned in the second law is the **net force** (the **vector sum** of all forces). If multiple forces act on an object but their sum is **zero**, the **acceleration** remains **zero**.
 
• **Real-world applications:** This principle is used in **automotive engineering** to determine **engine power**, in **aerospace** to calculate **rocket thrust**, and in **sports science** to analyze **athlete performance**.
 
• **Units:** Always ensure **mass** is in **kilograms** and **acceleration** is in **m/s²** to obtain the **force** in **Newtons**. **1 Newton = 1 kg·m/s²**.

questions.question: Aarti got a new bed at 50% discount. If Aarti did not get any discount, Aarti would have to pay ₹8,453 extra. So how much did Aarti pay for the bed?

Let the **Marked Price** be 100%.

Given **Discount** = 50%, so **Selling Price** = 100% − 50% = 50%.

The extra amount without discount represents the discount value itself.

Since 50% discount = ₹8,453, then the amount paid (50%) is also ₹8,453.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,453.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Discount % = 50%, Extra amount if no discount = ₹8,453.

**Formulas:** Discount = MP − SP | Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 | SP = MP − Discount

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0fed4ff1ed8795a5c78c4dd70b763d5cad8906de89fc2b520cd47597b4e56061.png]

⇒ Amount paid (SP) = MP − Discount = 16,906 − 8,453 = ₹8,453.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,453.**

**__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

The **Marked Price** is the price listed on the label. **Discount** is always calculated on the Marked Price unless stated otherwise.

The 50% Rule

When a **50% discount** is applied, the **Selling Price** and the **Discount Value** are always equal, as the price is split exactly in half.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 20% of the voters did not cast their votes, and all the votes cast were valid. The winner secured 70% of the votes cast and won by a margin of 23,200 votes. What was the total number of voters?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Total Voters** be 100%.

**Voters who cast votes** = 100% − 20% = 80%.

Winner gets 70% of 80%, Loser gets 30% of 80%.

**Difference** = (70% − 30%) of 80% = 40% of 80% = 32%.

32% = 23,200 ⇒ 1% = 725 ⇒ 100% = 72,500.

**∴ The correct answer is 72,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/432e3a5778dc1019e4fe0f741cdc65650911d1495d9a2f7e926b571168bb71e5.png] 

**Given:**

Non-voters = 20%

Winner share of cast votes = 70%

Winning margin = 23,200

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let total number of voters = **x**

⇒ Votes cast = 80% of **x** = 0.8x

⇒ Winner's votes = 70% of 0.8x = 0.56x

⇒ Loser's votes = (100% − 70%) of 0.8x = 30% of 0.8x = 0.24x

⇒ Margin = 0.56x − 0.24x = 0.32x

⇒ 0.32x = 23,200

⇒ x = 23,200 ÷ 0.32

⇒ x = 72,500

**∴ The correct answer is 72,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Invalid Votes Concept

If some votes are invalid, subtract them from the cast votes before calculating the winner's share: **Valid Votes = Cast Votes − Invalid Votes**.

Percentage Change

Margin percentage based on total voters is **(Winner% − Loser%) × (Cast Vote%)**.

Total Population vs Voters

Voters are usually a subset of the total population; questions may involve multiple stages of reduction from **Total Population** → **Voter List** → **Casted Votes**.</p

questions.question: A car travels a distance of 120 km in 2 hours. What is its speed?

**Speed** is distance per unit time.

Direct division: 120 ÷ 2 = 60 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Distance** = 120 km

**Time** = 2 hours

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69fb4da2fb41f3c6499a3a2bbf1cb9123d8775e05efb373619452149ec12bf0b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed = 120 km ÷ 2 hours

⇒ Speed = 60 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

Total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. For two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).</p

questions.question: An article is marked 25% above its cost price. A discount is offered so that a profit of 15% is made. Find the discount percentage.

Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 25% of 100 = 125.

**Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 15% of 100 = 115.

**Discount** = MP − SP = 125 − 115 = 10.

**Discount %** = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (10 ÷ 125) × 100 = 8%.

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Markup% = 25%, Profit% = 15%.
**Formulas:** MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 | Discount% = (MP − SP) ÷ MP × 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ebd5bb2711c42708da5e2738ad0d8598521de5841e24a5d7357af8b155111807.png] 
⇒ Assume CP = 100 units.
⇒ MP = 100 × (125 ÷ 100) = 125 units.
⇒ SP = 100 × (115 ÷ 100) = 115 units.
⇒ Discount Amount = MP − SP = 125 − 115 = 10 units.
⇒ Discount% = (10 ÷ 125) × 100 = 8%.

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. Formula: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Relation between CP and MP

The direct ratio is MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).</p

Base circumference (2πr) = 176 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 176 ÷ (2 × 22/7) = 28 cm.

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 176

⇒ (44/7) × r = 176

⇒ r = 176 × (7/44) = 4 × 7 = 28 cm

⇒ TSA = 2 × (22/7) × 28 × (56 + 28)

⇒ TSA = 176 × 84

⇒ TSA = 14,784 cm²

questions.question: From an interior point of an equilateral triangle, three perpendiculars are drawn to its three sides which are of lengths 12.7 cm, 14.8 cm and 11.5 cm, respectively. Find the area of the equilateral triangle.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For an **equilateral triangle**, the sum of **perpendicular distances** (p₁, p₂, p₃) from an interior point to the sides is equal to the **height** (h).

h = p₁ + p₂ + p₃ = 12.7 + 14.8 + 11.5 = 39 cm.

Area = h² / √3 = 39² / √3 = 1521 / √3 = 507√3 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 507√3 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Perpendiculars p₁ = 12.7 cm, p₂ = 14.8 cm, p₃ = 11.5 cm.

**Formula:** Sum of perpendiculars (p₁+p₂+p₃) = (√3/2) × side (a).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4ba81cfa2c887271d0614140470d3726e9b474ff5b7eeced7016628c054aa09f.png] 

⇒ Let the side of the **equilateral triangle** be 'a'.

⇒ Area of triangle = Sum of areas of three smaller triangles formed with the interior point.

⇒ (√3/4)a² = (1/2)×a×p₁ + (1/2)×a×p₂ + (1/2)×a×p₃

⇒ (√3/4)a² = (1/2)a (p₁ + p₂ + p₃)

⇒ (√3/2)a = 12.7 + 14.8 + 11.5 = 39

⇒ a = 78 / √3 = 26√3 cm

⇒ Area = (√3/4) × (26√3)²

⇒ Area = (√3/4) × 676 × 3 = 169 × 3 × √3 = 507√3 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 507√3 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Viviani's Theorem

It states that the sum of the distances from any interior point to the sides of an **equilateral triangle** is constant and equal to the **altitude** (h) of the triangle.

Equilateral Triangle Formulas

Height (h) = (√3/2)a; Area = (√3/4)a²; In-radius (r) = a/(2√3); Circum-radius (R) = a/√3.

Area in terms of Height

If the height 'h' is known, the area of an **equilateral triangle** can be directly calculated as Area = h² / √3.</p

questions.question: A taxi service charges a fixed base fare plus a variable rate per kilometre. For a 10 km trip, Raju paid ₹230 and for a 15 km trip, Meena paid ₹330. What is the base fare and the per-kilometre charge?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in **Distance** = 15 − 10 = 5 km

Difference in **Fare** = ₹330 − ₹230 = ₹100

**Per-kilometre Charge** = ₹100 ÷ 5 = ₹20 per km

**Base Fare** = Total Fare − (Distance × Per-km Charge) = 230 − (10 × 20) = ₹30

**∴ The correct answer is Base fare = ₹30; Per-kilometre Charge = ₹20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db2857c4617220f09d137824c2d0cc9e02691a89299c8e3a58c0390e5ea39ed2.png] 

**Given:**

Let **Base Fare** be 'B' and **Rate per km** be 'R'.

⇒ Case 1: B + 10R = 230 — (i)

⇒ Case 2: B + 15R = 330 — (ii)

**Calculations:**

Subtracting equation (i) from (ii):

⇒ (B + 15R) − (B + 10R) = 330 − 230

⇒ 5R = 100

⇒ R = 20

Substitute R = 20 in equation (i):

⇒ B + 10(20) = 230

⇒ B + 200 = 230

⇒ B = 30

**∴ The correct answer is Base fare = ₹30; Per-kilometre Charge = ₹20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equation Modeling

Simultaneous Equations

To find two unknowns, we require at least two independent linear equations. The **elimination method** is usually the fastest way to solve for the variable rate.

Unitary Application

In fixed plus variable cost problems, the **entire difference** in total cost is attributed to the **difference in variable quantity** only.
