questions.question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 3, 10 and 15 days, respectively. How long (in days) will they take to do twice the same work, working together?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Combined efficiency of **A, B and C** = (Total Work ÷ 3) + (Total Work ÷ 10) + (Total Work ÷ 15)

Using **LCM (3, 10, 15) = 30** as base work.

Total efficiency = 10 + 3 + 2 = 15 units/day.

**Twice the work** = 30 × 2 = 60 units.

Time taken = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A** = 3 days, **B** = 10 days, **C** = 15 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = LCM of individual days; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time; Time = Work ÷ Efficiency.

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 **A** 3 30 units 10 
 **B** 10 3 
 **C** 15 2 

⇒ **Combined efficiency** of (A + B + C) = 10 + 3 + 2 = 15 units/day.

⇒ **Original work** = 30 units.

⇒ **Twice the work** = 30 × 2 = 60 units.

⇒ **Required time** = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete a task. If time ratio is x : y, then efficiency ratio is y : x.

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar logic applies where **filling pipes** have positive efficiency and **leakage pipes** have negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the **ratio of work done** or the **ratio of efficiencies** when all persons work for the same duration.</p

questions.question: In a distribution where the empirical relation holds true, if both the mode and the median are 46, find the mean.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For any distribution following the **Empirical Relationship**, if the **Mode** and **Median** are equal, the **Mean** must also be equal to that same value.

Given: **Mode** = 46 and **Median** = 46.

Observation: Since **Mode** = **Median**, the distribution is considered symmetrical at this point, leading to **Mean** = 46.

**∴ The correct answer is 46.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Mode** = 46

⇒ **Median** = 46

**Formula Used:**

The **Empirical Relationship** between the three measures of central tendency is:

⇒ **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32108e9379e3852b526558c6ec9f9c540e9289e29d564f507d79aaad02a4e0a0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 46 = 3 × 46 − 2 × **Mean**

⇒ 46 = 138 − 2 × **Mean**

⇒ 2 × **Mean** = 138 − 46

⇒ 2 × **Mean** = 92

⇒ **Mean** = 92 ÷ 2

⇒ **Mean** = 46

**∴ The correct answer is 46.**

**__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

Karl Pearson's formula relates the three averages as: **Mode** = 3 **Median** − 2 **Mean**. It is applicable for moderately skewed distributions.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly **Symmetrical Distribution** (like the Normal Distribution), the values of **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all identical.

Skewed Distributions

For **Positively Skewed** data: **Mean** > **Median** > **Mode**. For **Negatively Skewed** data: **Mode** > **Median** > **Mean**.</p

questions.question: Expand: (3m - 5n)²
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **algebraic identity** (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².

Square of the **first term**: (3m)² = 9m².

Square of the **second term**: (5n)² = 25n².

The **middle term** is −2 × (3m) × (5n) = −30mn.

Combine all parts: 9m² − 30mn + 25n².

**∴ The correct answer is 9m² − 30mn + 25n².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (3m − 5n)²

**Formula Used:** **(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²**

⇒ Identifying values: **a = 3m** and **b = 5n**.

⇒ Expansion: (3m)² − 2 × (3m) × (5n) + (5n)²

⇒ (3 × 3 × m × m) − (2 × 3 × 5 × m × n) + (5 × 5 × n × n)

⇒ 9m² − 30mn + 25n²

⇒ This expression corresponds to **Option 4**.

**∴ The correct answer is 9m² − 30mn + 25n².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square of a Sum Identity

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b². The only difference is the sign of the **middle term**.

Difference of Two Squares

(a − b)(a + b) = a² − b². This is used for **factorization** and simplifying products.

Cubic expansion of Difference

(a − b)³ = a³ − 3a²b + 3ab² − b³. Note the **alternating signs** in the result.</p

questions.question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of angle R and angle S meet at the point T (inside the quadrilateral) and angle STR = 17^circ . If the ratio of angle P to angle Q is 8 : 9, then what is the difference between the measures of angle Q and angle P ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The angle formed by the bisectors of two adjacent angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the sum of the other two angles:

⇒ ∠STR = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2

⇒ 17° = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2 ⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 34°

Given ratio ∠P : ∠Q = 8 : 9, the sum of ratio parts is 8 + 9 = 17 units.

Difference between ∠Q and ∠P = 9 − 8 = 1 unit = 34° × (1 ÷ 17) = 2°.

**∴ The correct answer is 2°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ In **quadrilateral PQRS**, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at point **T**.

⇒ ∠STR = 17°

⇒ Ratio of ∠P to ∠Q = 8 : 9

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **Sum of interior angles** of a quadrilateral = 360°

⇒ **Sum of angles** in a triangle = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f813ebf3a3b15f65ffe03429170f49d8d7109f41dcc42b15b6bd50ed052c1670.png] 

**Calculations:**

In triangle **STR**:

⇒ ∠STR + ∠TSR + ∠TRS = 180°

Since **ST** and **RT** are the **angle bisectors** of ∠S and ∠R respectively:

⇒ ∠TSR = ∠S ÷ 2

⇒ ∠TRS = ∠R ÷ 2

Substituting these values into the triangle angle sum equation:

⇒ 17° + (∠S ÷ 2) + (∠R ÷ 2) = 180°

⇒ (∠S + ∠R) ÷ 2 = 180° − 17°

⇒ (∠S + ∠R) ÷ 2 = 163°

⇒ ∠S + ∠R = 326°

In quadrilateral **PQRS**, the sum of all interior angles is 360°:

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + ∠R + ∠S = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + 326° = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 360° − 326°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 34°

Given that the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 8 : 9, let ∠P = 8x and ∠Q = 9x:

⇒ 8x + 9x = 34°

⇒ 17x = 34°

⇒ x = 2°

The difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P is:

⇒ ∠Q − ∠P = 9x − 8x = x

⇒ x = 2°

**∴ The correct answer is 2°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Bisector Theorem in Quadrilaterals

The angle formed by the bisectors of two adjacent angles of a quadrilateral is always equal to half the sum of the remaining two opposite angles.

Sum of Interior Angles of a Polygon

For any convex polygon with n sides, the sum of all interior angles is given by the formula (n − 2) × 180°.</p

questions.question: Walking at (4)/(7) of his normal speed from his home, Shahid is 12 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **distance** is constant, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time**.

Speed Ratio (Usual : New) = 7 : 4 → Time Ratio (Usual : New) = 4 : 7.

Difference in time units = 7 − 4 = 3 units.

Given, 3 units = 12 minutes ⇒ 1 unit = 4 minutes.

Usual Time = 4 units × 4 minutes = 16 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** New Speed = 4/7 of **Normal Speed**, Delay = 12 minutes.

**Formula Used:** Usual Time = [Late time × Numerator] ÷ [Difference between Numerator and Denominator]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20ed903adb0852d8340bac79fcf7a9cc01c95eee429f3da26bacd461cb5a6de8.png] 

⇒ Let Usual Speed be S and Usual Time be T.

⇒ Distance D = S × T

⇒ New Speed = 4/7 S, New Time = T + 12

⇒ D = (4/7 S) × (T + 12)

⇒ S × T = 4/7 S × (T + 12)

⇒ 7T = 4T + 48

⇒ 3T = 48

⇒ T = 16 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportionality Rule

If Speed becomes a/b of its original value, the Time taken becomes b/a of the original time.

Average Speed

Average speed for equal distances at different speeds x and y is given by 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their speeds.</p

questions.question: The price of an article is first increased by 20% and later on, it is decreased by 25% due to reduction in sales. Find the net percentage change in final price of the article.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Apply the **successive percentage change** formula: Net Change = a + b + (a × b)/100

Given: a = +20% (increase) and b = −25% (decrease)

Net Change = 20 − 25 + (20 × (−25))/100

Net Change = −5 − 5 = −10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10% decrease.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First increase = 20%, Second decrease = 25%

**Formula Used:** Final Price = Initial Price × (100 + %change₁)/100 × (100 + %change₂)/100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b92a67f92cebef911e56da8f21209fce158f2f9ee442a255b46c6616e4c633f.png] 
⇒ Let the **initial price** be 100 units.

⇒ Price after 20% **increase** = 100 + 20% of 100 = 120 units.

⇒ Price after 25% **decrease** = 120 − 25% of 120

⇒ 120 − (25/100 × 120) = 120 − 30 = 90 units.

⇒ Net change = 100 − 90 = 10 units.

⇒ Net percentage change = (10/100) × 100 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10% decrease.**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by x% and then by y%, the effective change is (x + y + xy/100)%. Use positive for increase and negative for decrease.

Fractional Conversion

20% increase is a multiplier of 6/5 and 25% decrease is a multiplier of 3/4. Net multiplier = 6/5 × 3/4 = 18/20 = 9/10, which indicates a 1/10 or 10% decrease.

Product Stability

If an item price increases by x%, the consumption must decrease by [x/(100+x)] × 100 to keep the expenditure constant.</p

questions.question: The market prices of jowar to gram are in the ratio 1 : 5, and a family consumes them in the ratio 4 : 3 by quantity. Find the ratio of expenditure on jowar to that on gram.

questions.question: A stationery seller purchases 6 notebooks for ₹30 and sells them for ₹36. What is his profit percentage?

questions.question: The average age of 43 students of a class is 25 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 26 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Teacher's Age** = **New Average** + (**Old Count** × **Increase in Average**)

Given: **Old Average** = 25 years | **New Average** = 26 years

**Old Count** = 43 students | **Increase** = 26 − 25 = 1 year

⇒ **Teacher's Age** = 26 + (43 × 1) = 26 + 43 = 69 years

**∴ The correct answer is 69 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number of **students** = 43, **Average age** = 25 years, **Average** with **teacher** included = 26 years.

**Formula Used:** Total Sum = Average × Number of Observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de64777d6357ec0aead62f6ae93a117defb8352db8e465e61bbc923e06a92bca.png] 

⇒ **Total age of 43 students** = 43 × 25 = 1075 years

⇒ **Total persons** (including teacher) = 43 + 1 = 44

⇒ **Total age of 44 persons** = 44 × 26 = 1144 years

⇒ **Teacher's age** = (**Total age of 44 persons**) − (**Total age of 43 students**)

⇒ **Teacher's age** = 1144 − 1075 = 69 years

**∴ The correct answer is 69 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

General Inclusion Formula

Value of new entry = (New Number of items × New Average) − (Old Number of items × Old Average).

Net Deviation Method

Sum of deviations from the average is always zero. If the average increases, the new value must be greater than the old average by (Total New Count × Increase).

Average of Groups

Combined Average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the count and x is the average of each group.</p

questions.question: A garrison of 1209 men has provisions for 20 days. How long (in days) will the provisions last if the garrison is increased by 403 men?

1209 × 20 = 1612 × D₂

D₂ = (1209 × 20) ÷ 1612 = 15 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

⇒ D₂ = (1209 × 20) ÷ 1612

⇒ D₂ = 24180 ÷ 1612

Chain Rule (Inverse Proportion)

questions.question: The price of fuel decreases by 45%, 15% and 50% in three successive months, but increases by 70% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price? (Rounded off to two decimal places)

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **multiplying factor** method for **successive changes**.

Net multiplier = (1 − 0.45) × (1 − 0.15) × (1 − 0.50) × (1 + 0.70)

Net multiplier = 0.55 × 0.85 × 0.50 × 1.70 = 0.397375

Decrease % = (1 − 0.397375) × 100 = 60.2625%

**∴ The correct answer is Decreases by 60.26%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Initial price of **fuel** = 100 units

Successive changes: **45% decrease**, **15% decrease**, **50% decrease**, and **70% increase**.

⇒ Price after 2nd month = 55 × (85/100) = 46.75

⇒ Price after 3rd month = 46.75 × (50/100) = 23.375

⇒ Price after 4th month = 23.375 × (170/100) = 39.7375

⇒ Net Change = Final Price − Original Price = 39.7375 − 100 = −60.2625

⇒ Percentage Change = (−60.2625 / 100) × 100 = −60.2625%

**∴ The correct answer is Decreases by 60.26%.**

For two changes x% and y%, the net change is given by the formula: [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Base Value Change

Percentage increase/decrease is always calculated on the **preceding value** in a successive series, not the original 100 throughout.

Multiplying Factor

questions.question: Which of the following Constitution Amendment Bills was introduced in the Lok Sabha in August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**130th Amendment Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **130th Constitution Amendment Bill** was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** in **August 2025** to address specific socio-political and administrative requirements regarding the categorization of communities.
 
• This bill primarily focuses on the **modification of the list of Scheduled Tribes** in certain states, specifically aimed at ensuring that marginalized communities receive the benefits of reservation and social welfare schemes.
 
• The introduction of such bills is usually handled by the **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** or the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**, depending on the specific community being addressed.
 
• The **130th Amendment Bill** seeks to amend the **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950**, which is the primary legal instrument defining which communities are recognized as STs in various states of India.
 
• By being introduced in the **lower house of Parliament (Lok Sabha)**, the bill follows the legislative procedure outlined under **Article 368** of the Constitution, although amendments to the ST list specifically follow the procedure under **Article 342**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Procedure for Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• As per **Article 368**, an amendment of the Constitution can be initiated only by the introduction of a Bill for the purpose in either House of **Parliament**.
 
• The Bill must be passed in each House by a **special majority**, which is a majority of the total membership of that House and a majority of not less than **two-thirds** of the members of that House present and voting.
 
• There is **no provision for a joint sitting** in case of a deadlock between the two Houses over a Constitutional Amendment Bill.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Tribes and Article 342:**
 
 
• **Article 342** of the Indian Constitution empowers the **President** to specify the tribes or tribal communities which shall be deemed to be Scheduled Tribes in relation to a State or Union Territory.
 
• However, any inclusion or exclusion from the list of Scheduled Tribes after the initial notification can only be done by an **Act of Parliament**.
 
• This process ensures that changes to the tribal status of a community undergo rigorous **legislative scrutiny** and debate within the **Lok Sabha** and **Rajya Sabha**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 130th Bill:**
 
 
• The bill is significant for communities like the **Hattee community** (often associated with Himachal Pradesh) or similar groups who have long-standing demands for **ST status** to improve their socio-economic standing.
 
• Granting ST status provides access to **institutional reservations** in educational institutions and government jobs, as well as protection under the **Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989**.
 
 
 
• **Difference between Bills and Acts:**
 
 
• A **Bill** is a draft legislative proposal that becomes an **Act** only after it has been passed by both Houses of Parliament and received the **assent of the President**.
 
• The numbering of **Amendment Bills** is continuous and often differs from the numbering of **Amendment Acts** because not every bill introduced in Parliament successfully becomes law.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the Registrar General of India (RGI):** Before a community is added to the ST list via an amendment bill, the proposal must be vetted by the **Registrar General of India** and the **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST)**.
 
• **Socio-Economic Criteria:** The criteria used to define a community as a Scheduled Tribe include **primitive traits**, distinctive culture, **geographical isolation**, shyness of contact with the community at large, and **backwardness**.
 
• **Legislative Timeline:** While the **128th Amendment Act** (Women's Reservation) was a major milestone in **2023**, the sequence of subsequent bills like the 129th and **130th** demonstrates the government's ongoing focus on **social inclusion** and administrative adjustments.

The correct answer is __**5.6%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** data indicates that the **unemployment rate** in India for the period of **May 2025** stood at **5.6%**.
 
• The **unemployment rate (UR)** is calculated as the percentage of persons unemployed among the total persons in the **labour force**.
 
• The **PLFS** is an initiative by the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)**, which functions under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** of the **Government of India**.
 
• The primary objective of the **PLFS** is to estimate the key employment and unemployment indicators such as the **Worker Population Ratio (WPR)**, **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)**, and **Unemployment Rate (UR)** in a short time interval of three months for **urban areas** only in the **Current Weekly Status (CWS)**.

• **Child Wasting**: This indicates the share of **children under age five** who have low weight for their height, reflecting **acute undernutrition**.

__
 
• The **Mussalman Wakf (Repeal) Bill, 2025**, was introduced to formally repeal the **Mussalman Wakf Act, 1923**, a colonial-era legislation that had become redundant following the enactment of more comprehensive laws.
 
• This Bill received the **Presidential assent** in **January 2025**, following its passage in both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha** during the legislative sessions focusing on **Waqf reforms**.
 
• The primary objective of this repeal was to remove the **obsolete 1923 Act** from the statute books, as its provisions regarding the submission of accounts by **Mutawallis** were already covered under the **Waqf Act, 1995**.
 
• The repeal process was carried out alongside the **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024**, which sought to bring significant transparency and accountability to the management of **Waqf properties** across **India**.
 
• The **Ministry of Minority Affairs** spearheaded these legislative changes to streamline the administration of religious endowments and ensure better utilization of land for community welfare. ***Hence, the correct answer is Mussalman Wakf (Repeal) Bill.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Waqf Act, 1995:**

 
 
• This is the principal legislation governing **Waqf** in **India**. It provides for the establishment of **State Waqf Boards** and the **Central Waqf Council**.
 
• The **2024-2025 reforms** proposed renaming this act to the **Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Act**.
 
• The Act defines **Waqf** as the permanent dedication of any movable or immovable property for purposes recognized by **Muslim Law** as pious, religious, or charitable.
 
 
 
• **Waqf Boards and Governance:**
 
 
• Every **State** in **India** has a **Waqf Board**, which is a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal.
 
• The **Mutawalli** is the person who manages the **Waqf property**, but they are overseen by the **State Waqf Board** to prevent mismanagement.
 
• The new amendments aim to include **Muslim women** and **non-Muslims** in these boards to increase diversity and professional oversight.
 
 
 
• **The Mussalman Wakf Act, 1923:**
 
 
• This **British-era** law was limited in scope, focusing mainly on the obligation of managers to furnish statements of particulars and accounts to the **District Court**.
 
• Because the **1995 Act** provided a much more robust mechanism for audits and judicial oversight through **Waqf Tribunals**, the **1923 Act** was no longer necessary.

• The committee held several meetings across **India**, including locations like **Mumbai**, **Ahmedabad**, and **Delhi**, to gather feedback from stakeholders, including **All India Muslim Personal Law Board** and various **Sufi** organizations.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the 2025 Reform Era:**
 
 
• **Digitization**: A centralized portal (**WAMSI**) is being enhanced to map all **Waqf properties** using **GIS technology** to prevent encroachments.
 
• **Audit Requirements**: The new reforms mandate that **Waqf** accounts must be audited by **auditors** appointed by the **State Government** or the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)** in certain cases.
 
• **Tribunal Powers**: The **Waqf Tribunals** have been restructured to ensure that disputes regarding **property titles** are settled within a stipulated **timeframe of 6 months to 1 year**.

questions.question: Which of the following Bills, presented by the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation on 20 August 2025, prohibits individuals holding key constitutional offices from administering the government while in jail?

options.text: Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2025
Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Seventh Amendment) Bill, 2025
Constitution (One Hundred and Thirtieth Amendment) Bill, 2025
Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2025

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Constitution (One Hundred and Thirtieth Amendment) Bill, 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **20 August 2025**, the **Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation** presented the **Constitution (One Hundred and Thirtieth Amendment) Bill, 2025** in the Parliament.
 
• The primary objective of this **legislative measure** is to prohibit individuals holding **key constitutional offices**, such as **Chief Ministers** or **Union Ministers**, from administering the government or exercising executive functions while being held in **judicial custody** or **jail**.
 
• This bill seeks to address a **legal lacuna** regarding the ethical and administrative feasibility of a **government-in-absentia**, ensuring that the dignity of the **Constitutional office** is maintained.
 
• The **amendment** introduces specific clauses that mandate the **immediate vacation** of office or the appointment of an **officiating authority** if the incumbent is remanded to **jail** for a period exceeding a specified duration.
 
• By barring governance from **prison**, the bill aims to uphold the **sanctity of the Constitution** and ensure that **public administration** remains transparent and accessible to the citizenry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Framework for Amendments:**

 
 
• Under **Article 368** of the **Indian Constitution**, the **Parliament** has the power to amend the Constitution by way of addition, variation, or repeal of any provision.
 
• A **Constitution Amendment Bill** like the **130th Amendment** requires a **special majority** in both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha** to be passed.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Integrity:**
 
 
• The concept of **administrative integrity** implies that those in **executive power** must be able to perform their **statutory duties** without physical or legal constraints that hinder **governance**.
 
• Prior to this **2025 bill**, there was no explicit **Constitutional provision** that automatically disqualified a **Minister** or **Chief Minister** from continuing in office solely due to being in **custody**, provided they had not been **convicted** of a crime.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Home Ministry:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)**, led by the **Union Home Minister**, is responsible for matters relating to the **internal security**, **inter-state relations**, and the administration of **Union Territories**.
 
• Introducing such **amendments** often falls under the purview of the **MHA** when they relate to the **structural integrity** of the **Indian state** and **legal governance**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Bill:**

 
 
• The **Constitution (One Hundred and Thirtieth Amendment) Bill** is a landmark move to prevent **political instability** caused by leaders attempting to run **state machinery** from **confinement**.
 
• It reinforces the **principle of accountability**, ensuring that those who cannot physically attend **Cabinet meetings** or access **classified documents** due to **incarceration** cannot hold the **reins of power**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Representation of the People Act:**
 
 
• While the **Representation of the People Act, 1951** deals with the **disqualification** of **MPs** and **MLAs** upon **conviction** (usually for **2 years** or more), this new **Amendment** focuses specifically on the **custodial stage** for **Constitutional heads**.
 
• It distinguishes between the **right to represent** a constituency and the **executive authority** to lead a **government**.

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, in **January 2025**, lifted the supervisory restrictions on **Arohan Financial Services**, allowing the firm to resume its **sanction and disbursement** of loans.

• The **central bank** had observed that the **Weighted Average Lending Rate (WALR)** and the interest margins charged by the company were significantly higher than the benchmarks, violating **Fair Practices Code** guidelines.
 
• Alongside **Arohan Financial Services**, the **RBI** also removed similar curbs on **Asirvad Microfinance** and **DMI Finance** in early **January 2025** after they demonstrated improvement in their pricing policies.

• **Regulatory Framework for NBFCs:**
 
 
• The **RBI** exercises its powers under **Section 45L(1)(b)** of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, to issue directions to **Non-Banking Financial Companies** to ensure financial stability.
 
• In **2024**, the **RBI** intensified its scrutiny on the **microfinance sector** to prevent **excessive interest rates** and ensure that the benefits of low-cost funding are passed to **low-income borrowers**.
 
 
 
• **Arohan Financial Services:**

• The organization primarily focuses on providing **credit facilities** to women in **rural and semi-urban** areas for income-generating activities.
 
 
 
• **The October 2024 Action:**
 
 
• In a rare move, the **RBI** had simultaneously barred **four NBFCs**—**Navi Finserv**, **Asirvad Microfinance**, **Arohan Financial Services**, and **DMI Finance**—from loan disbursements.
 
• The action was part of a broader **supervisory campaign** to curb **irresponsible lending** and ensure that **digital lenders** and **MFIs** maintain **transparency** in their **Annual Percentage Rate (APR)**.

• **Impact of Curbs:** The imposition of curbs usually leads to a temporary halt in **Asset Under Management (AUM)** growth and affects the **liquidity** and **credit ratings** of the concerned entities.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**August 12**__.

__
 
• **International Youth Day** is observed annually on **August 12** across the globe to recognize the efforts of the world's youth in enhancing global society.
 
• The **United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)** officially designated this day in **December 1999**, following recommendations made by the **World Conference of Ministers Responsible for Youth** held in **Lisbon** in **August 1998**.
 
• The very first International Youth Day was celebrated on **August 12, 2000**, serving as an opportunity for governments and others to draw attention to youth issues worldwide.
 
• The observance aims to promote ways to engage young people in becoming more actively involved in making positive contributions to their communities and participating in **social, economic, and political life**.
 
• Each year, the **United Nations** selects a specific theme for the day; for example, the **2024** theme was **"From Clicks to Progress: Youth Digital Pathways for Sustainable Development,"** highlighting the role of digitalization in achieving **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Youth Day (India):**
 
 
• In **India**, **National Youth Day** is celebrated on **January 12** every year.
 
• This date was chosen to honor the birth anniversary of **Swami Vivekananda**, one of India's greatest spiritual and social leaders, who had immense faith in the power of youth.
 
• The government of India declared this day as National Youth Day in **1984**, and it was first celebrated in **1985**.
 
 
 
• **Defining "Youth":**
 
 
• The **United Nations** defines "youth" as those persons between the ages of **15 and 24** years for statistical purposes without prejudice to other definitions by **Member States**.
 
• Currently, there are **1.2 billion** young people aged **15 to 24** years, accounting for **16 percent** of the global population.
 
• By **2030**—the target date for the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**—the number of youth is projected to have grown by **7 percent**, to nearly **1.3 billion**.
 
 
 
• **Global Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **UN Youth Strategy (Youth2030)** was launched in **2018** to facilitate increased impact and expanded action to address the needs of young people.
 
• The **Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC)** Youth Forum is an annual event that provides a platform for young people to engage in a dialogue with **Member States** on global policy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Important Dates:**
 
 
• **August 9:** Observed as the **International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples**.
 
• **September 21:** Recognized as the **International Day of Peace** (World Peace Day).
 
• **July 18:** Celebrated as **Nelson Mandela International Day** to honor the legacy of the former South African President.
 
 
 
• **Thematic Focus:** International Youth Day often focuses on critical areas such as **education**, **employment**, **environment**, **mental health**, and **civic engagement** to empower the younger generation for a better future.

questions.question: The Environment Audit Rules, 2025, were introduced by which ministry in India?

options.text: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** is the nodal agency in the administrative structure of the **Central Government** for the planning, promotion, co-ordination and overseeing the implementation of **India's** environmental and forestry policies and programmes.
 
• The **Environment Audit Rules, 2025**, were introduced to streamline and standardize the process of environmental auditing for industries and infrastructure projects that require **Environmental Clearance (EC)** under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**.
 
• The primary objective of these rules is to ensure that industrial units and project proponents comply with the environmental safeguards and conditions prescribed during the grant of clearance, thereby promoting **sustainable development**.
 
• The rules introduce a framework for **Third-Party Audits**, where registered environmental auditors evaluate the performance of an organization’s environmental management system and its impact on the **ecosystem**.
 
• Under the **2025 Rules**, it is mandatory for specified categories of industries to submit an **Annual Environmental Audit Report** to the respective **State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)** and the **MoEFCC**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC):**
 
 
• Established in its current form in **1985**, it oversees the implementation of various landmark legislations including the **Wildlife Protection Act (1972)**, the **Water Act (1974)**, and the **Air Act (1981)**.
 
• The ministry is responsible for **Climate Change** negotiations at the international level, such as the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)** and **COP** summits.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA):**
 
 
• This ministry is primarily concerned with the administration of the **Companies Act, 2013** and the **Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008**.
 
• It regulates corporate governance and **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)** activities, but does not directly issue environmental audit rules for ecological compliance.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Commerce & Industry:**
 
 
• Administers the **Department of Commerce** and the **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**.
 
• It focuses on **foreign trade**, **Special Economic Zones (SEZs)**, and **industrial policy** to enhance **Ease of Doing Business** in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES):**
 
 
• Formed in **2006**, it deals with **oceanography**, **meteorology**, **seismology**, and **polar science**.
 
• It manages the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** and focuses on predicting weather, climate, and ocean state, rather than industrial environmental auditing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Framework:** The **Environment Audit Rules, 2025** function under the overarching powers of the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**, which allows the **Central Government** to take all such measures as it deems necessary for protecting and improving the quality of the environment.
 
• **Accreditation of Auditors:** The rules specify that only auditors accredited by the **National Accreditation Board for Education and Training (NABET)** or the **Quality Council of India (QCI)** are authorized to conduct these statutory audits.
 
• **Penalty for Non-Compliance:** Failure to submit the audit report or providing false information can attract penalties under **Section 15** of the **Environment (Protection) Act**, which includes **imprisonment** for a term which may extend to **five years** or a **fine** up to **one lakh rupees**, or both.
 
• **Digital Integration:** The **2025 Rules** emphasize the use of the **PARIVESH** portal (Pro-Active and Responsive facilitation by Interactive, Virtuous and Environmental Single-window Hub) for the digital submission and tracking of audit reports to ensure **transparency**.
